title: Almond Turrón de Alicante
summary: Crunchy Spanish honey nougat cooked to 150 °C and packed with warm toasted whole almonds, cut into bars.

ingredients.item: neutral oil, for the tin and tools
egg white (from 1 large egg), pasteurised if you like
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Line the tin
steps.text: Line the tin with baking paper and brush it lightly with oil. Oil a second sheet of paper for the top as well.

steps.title: Toast the almonds
steps.text: Toast the almonds on the tray at 160 °C for 10-12 min, until pale gold when you cut one open. Turn the oven off and leave them inside to keep warm.

steps.title: Boil the syrup
steps.text: Put the sugar, honey and water in the saucepan over medium heat and stir until dissolved. Boil without stirring until it reads 121 °C, 3-4 min.

steps.title: Whip the egg white
steps.text: Meanwhile whisk the egg white with the salt in the mixer until it holds soft peaks.

steps.title: Add the syrup
steps.text: With the mixer on medium-high, pour in the hot syrup in a thin stream down the side of the bowl and whisk for 2 min, until thick and glossy.

steps.title: Cook it down
steps.text: Scrape the mixture back into the saucepan and stir constantly over medium-low heat for 20-30 min. It is ready when it is thick, light golden and reads 150 °C.

steps.title: Add the almonds
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat and quickly stir in the lemon zest and the warm almonds.

steps.title: Press
steps.text: Scrape into the tin, lay the oiled paper on top and press down hard and evenly with a flat-bottomed glass or your hands.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: Leave for 30 min, until just firm but still slightly warm, then lift out and cut into 16 bars with the heavy knife. Leave to cool completely, about 1 h.

tips: The most common mistake is stopping before 150 °C; the turrón will then be chewy instead of crunchy.
Stir constantly while cooking down or the bottom will scorch.
Egg safety: the egg white is cooked to 150 °C, well above 71 °C; pasteurised egg white also works.
If it sets too hard to cut, warm the slab in a 120 °C oven for 2-3 min.
storage: Wrap tightly and keep in an airtight container at cool room temperature for up to 3 weeks.
